building-032.png.generation_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: one transparent HD pixel-art building sprite for a display-only overlay of Colonization (1994).
Image 1 is the edit target and exact geometry reference: the original 23 by 27 pixel fur trader's house enlarged by nearest neighbour. Image 2 is the USER APPROVED fine pixel-art style reference only.
Redraw ONLY the building in Image 1 using the crisp pixel clusters, restrained warm earthy colors, stone/wood/shingle textures and lighting of Image 2. Closely retain Image 1's silhouette, projected angle, proportions, roof slopes and the exact placement and height of its two tall narrow upper projections. Keep the broad lower rectangular facade and its existing dark openings in the same positions. The goal is a small faithful house with more legible material detail, not a large landmark.
Use a real transparent background. Keep the building aligned within its original 23:27 canvas aspect ratio, with the same top/bottom/left/right extents and transparent gaps. The intended final display is 92 by 108 pixels, so use pixel-art detail that survives that size. No antialiased outlines, smooth painting or photorealism. No lettering, frame, ground tile, detached objects, new floors, balconies, arches, towers, people or extra scenery. Do not include any content from the style-reference sheet other than its visual style. Preserve the dark-to-light arrangement and the narrow organic green patches already in the target; do not grow them beyond the original silhouette.

sea-148.png.alpha: fully opaque; clip to verified per-pixel ownership on the main canvas
sea-148.png.generation_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one fully opaque seamless ocean texture for a 64 by 64 pixel display-only HD tile in Colonization (1994).
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target, our previously generated ocean v2. Image 2 is the user-approved fine pixel-art concept sheet, STYLE REFERENCE ONLY.
Primary request: adjust ONLY the ocean palette and microcontrast of Image 1 so that the ocean meets the restrained indigo coast of the existing game display. Preserve the square framing, top-down view, texture scale, and fine pixel-art character. Do not introduce a new art style.
Color palette: a narrow, subdued deep indigo palette centered on RGB (25,30,127), hexadecimal #191E7F. Dark ripple colors around RGB (16,22,117), lit ripple clusters around RGB (32,44,138). Most of the tile must remain close to the base indigo. Remove the electric royal-blue/cyan appearance and conspicuous bright sparkles of Image 1. No white highlights. Avoid bright teal, saturated cyan, or black patches. This is calm open water, with small subtle broken horizontal ripple clusters.
Style/medium: crisp, deliberately placed fine pixel clusters in the style of Image 2. Low contrast so that repeating the texture does not compete with tiny map buildings or labels. The texture must still read as detailed water at the intended 64 by 64 display size.
Composition/framing: one single square, uniform top-down open-water tile, seamless on all four edges. Even illumination. No large dark/light regions, vignette, directional lighting, border, horizon, shore, land, foam bands, ships, objects, text, icons, or sheet of multiple tiles. Do not copy any scenery from Image 2.
Constraints: all pixels opaque; edge-to-edge ocean; retain pixel art; no smooth painting, blur, anti-aliased outlines, photorealism, grid, labels, watermark, or decorative frame.
